name: legit_spike
about: Three legitimate spikes of three hundred milliseconds, very intense and entirely innocent: a cache purge lands and every edge asks the origin at once, a thundering herd that resolves itself in under half a second. Each spike is shorter than the stabilisation the retuned ladder allows between rungs, which is the point - it is aimed at the assumption that a gate measured in slow ticks is safe because a false positive would have to persist. A spike does not persist. It arrives inside one tick, and a ladder that climbs on a single tick of demand sees a demand as high as any attack would produce. The reverse proxy behind it reaches thirty-two hundred packets per second, three times entry_per_sec, from one address in the unified list. Between the spikes the traffic returns to an ordinary floor, so a ladder that does climb has no reason to come back down before the next one arrives - three chances to accumulate what one alone could not.

timeline.note: four seconds of the ordinary floor

phases.note: 300 ms thundering herd: every edge asks the origin at once
1.7 s back at the floor, not long enough to unwind a rung

timeline.note: ten seconds of quiet, long enough for any rung taken to be visible in the hold column
